title: Gameplay footage. What do you guys think?
author: Bhumph_
selftext: Here is a hoverboard racing game that I am developing right now its in a single player playtest phase with plans for multiplayer. Let me know what yall think

comments.author: techtimee
comments.body: Pretty impressive! Did you use Opus and Unity?

replies.author: Bhumph_
replies.body: godot, and gpt

replies.author: techtimee
replies.body: It looks really polished and unique visually. I think you've got something good going!

replies.author: Bhumph_
replies.body: Well there is some jank in the movement. but, I'm running into the problem of being to good at  it and cant tell if my partner is just bad at racing games ( skill issue) or there is a genuine need for change in the movement. I'm running a free playtest if you have the time to check it out!

replies.author: Hollow-Saint
replies.body: How are you planning to address the 'jank' in the movement?

replies.author: Bhumph_
replies.body: I have a playtest open on my patreon and [itch.io](http://itch.io) in hopes to get some feedback on what new players are struggling with. Although no one tried it yet.

replies.author: Bhumph_
replies.body: [https://blazer-mk1.itch.io/formula-h](https://blazer-mk1.itch.io/formula-h)

comments.author: passyourownbutter

replies.body: Gpt image gen, to meshy, to astra for final clean up, I posed model and guided the animation.

replies.body: I had that thought too. I can play around with the speed. thanks for the input

comments.author: Super-Award-2244
comments.body: Models and the sense of speed seem good. The animations are a bit rigid though. For the front flip I'd suggest lowering the "point of rotation" to something like between the character's legs. To have it at the height of the head is not physically possible and it breaks a bit the immersion

replies.author: Bhumph_
replies.body: completely agree!

comments.author: EnumeratedArray
comments.body: Computer players seem far too easy. They were gone after a few seconds

replies.author: Bhumph_
replies.body: Haha yes they are😂 I’ve been working on making them faster.

comments.author: darkoblivion000
comments.body:
Hi looks really nice!

Just a few comments from watching the video

\- looks like maybe inconsistency with impact detection as the bot clips the player from the right in the beginning and clips right through but then they come from the left and that time it detects the bump

\- the bubble force field obviously needs shading and depth but I’m sure you’re working on that

\- something about the track and lighting makes it feel not quite solid? Like obv you have lighting and a nice sunset going on and I see many objects having shadows but the track just looks flat and uniformly lit in all angles and it feels flat that way. Esp then halfway through the video there’s a section of track under the loop where you see the bottom of it and it’s just black - complete void. Makes it look a little unfinished

\- when the player lands you could maybe make it animate a little bit like bending knees to absorb the impact or something to increase immersion in the physics of the world feeling tangible

Looks great good luck!

replies.author: Bhumph_
replies.body:
Very good notes!

The AI bots need some work. It’s partly because I added that ramp in the beginning and that one bot hasn’t been updated😂

Yes you are right,  all of the items are function only and I’m am working on visuals for them

Lighting hasn’t been something I have taken into account much. This is really just a poorly done track  visually. I wanted a simple track that tests movement tech for people if they playtest it. I am working on a few track designs that should be much better visually. Thank you pointing it out to me!

I am in progress doing an animation overhaul. 

Thank you for all of your notes!!

replies.author: darkoblivion000
replies.body:
I think it already looks better and more buttoned up than a lot of other stuff posted here, so keep it up!

Maybe in a month or two my game will be in a state where I’m ready to share lol

comments.author: nedelll
comments.body: How did you get the sounds/models?

replies.author: Bhumph_
replies.body: Honestly the sounds/models are temporary, this is just a proof of concept just to get some feedback on the movement system. I wanted to go and hire artist for the sounds and models if there is enough demand for a game like this.
